akhfash:2-2.t: He said ﴿يَدْخُلُونَ فِي دِينِ ٱللَّهِ أَفْوَاجاً﴾: their singular is الفَوْج (a troop).

akhfash:3-3.t: And He said ﴿َفسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ﴾: He means "let your glorification be with praise" (يَكُونُ تسبيحُك بالحَمْد), because "التَسْبيح" (glorification) is remembrance (dhikr); so He said: "let your remembrance be with praise for what I have given you, the conquest of Mecca and other things". And a man says "قَضَيْتُ سُبْحتي من الذكر" ("I have completed my subḥa of remembrance").

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿إِذَا جَاءَ نَصْرُ اللَّهِ﴾ for His Prophet ﷺ against his enemies ﴿وَالْفَتْحُ﴾: the conquest of Mecca,

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وَرَأَيْتَ النَّاسَ يَدْخُلُونَ فِي دِينِ اللَّهِ﴾, that is, Islam, ﴿أَفْوَاجًا﴾: in groups, after they used to enter it one by one. That was after the conquest of Mecca, when the Arabs came to him from all regions of the land, obedient.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ﴾, that is, accompanied by His praise, ﴿وَاسْتَغْفِرْهُ إِنَّهُ كَانَ تَوَّابًا﴾. After the revelation of this sūra he ﷺ used to say often: "Glory be to Allah and with His praise; I seek Allah's forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance." From it he knew that his appointed time had drawn near. The conquest of Mecca was in Ramaḍān of the year eight, and he ﷺ died in Rabīʿ al-Awwal of the year ten.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿إِذا﴾ adverbial (ẓarfiyya), conditional, non-jussive. ﴿جاءَ نَصْرُ اللَّهِ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَالْفَتْحُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿وَرَأَيْتَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿النَّاسَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa) to what precedes it. ﴿يَدْخُلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. ﴿فِي دِينِ اللَّهِ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿أَفْواجاً﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿فَسَبِّحْ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb) of إذا, with no grammatical position. ﴿بِحَمْدِ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَاسْتَغْفِرْهُ﴾ an imperative verb and its object, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa) to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿كانَ﴾ kāna and its latent noun. ﴿تَوَّاباً﴾ its khabar (predicate); the verbal clause is the khabar of inna. The nominal clause is causal (taʿlīl), with no grammatical position.

dervis-irab:1-3.t:
* I'rab:
(إِذا جاءَ نَصْرُ اللَّهِ وَالْفَتْحُ) إذا is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition, attached to سبّح, which is its apodosis; the clause جاء is in the position of the genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; نصر الله is the fāʿil (agent) of جاء; and الفتح is conjoined to نصر. The maṣdar (verbal noun) is annexed to its agent, and its object is omitted, i.e. "you and the believers". Abū Ḥayyān said: It is not correct to make فسبّح operate on إذا because of the فاء, since in an apodosis of a condition the verb after the فاء does not govern the conditional noun, so it does not operate on it; rather, the operator on إذا is the verb that follows it, according to the sound view. (وَرَأَيْتَ النَّاسَ يَدْخُلُونَ فِي دِينِ اللَّهِ أَفْواجاً) The wāw is a conjunction; رأيت is a past verb with its agent; الناس is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The seeing may be of the eye, in which case the clause يدخلون is a ḥāl (circumstantial); or it may be of knowing, in which case the clause is the second mafʿūl bihi of رأيت. في دين الله is attached to يدخلون, and أفواجا is a ḥāl from the wāw in يدخلون; it is the plural of فوج (with sukūn on the wāw), whose explanation has already preceded. (فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ وَاسْتَغْفِرْهُ إِنَّهُ كانَ تَوَّاباً) The فاء links to the apodosis; سبّح is an imperative verb, its agent a pronoun obligatorily latent in it, its implied form being "you"; and بحمد ربك is a ḥāl. There has been a difference about the باء. It was said: it is for accompaniment, and الحمد is annexed to its object, i.e. "glorify Him while praising Him": declare Him exalted above what does not befit Him and affirm for Him what befits Him, so it is within the scope of the command. If you ask: from where does the command to praise follow, when it occurs only as a ḥāl restricting the glorification, and a command to do something does not entail a command regarding the state that restricts it? The answer is that this follows only when the ḥāl is not of the same kind as the commanded act and not of the act of the commanded person, as in "strike Hind laughing"; otherwise it does follow, as in "enter Mecca in a state of iḥrām", where it is commanded; and this case is of that type. It was also said: it is for seeking help, and الحمد is annexed to the agent, i.e. "glorify Him with that by which He praised Himself", as in His words الحمد لله. واستغفره: the wāw is a conjunction; استغفره is an imperative verb with a latent agent and an attached object. The clause إنه كان توّابا is explanatory of the reason (taʿlīliyya): إن with its noun, the clause كان being its khabar, and توّابا is the khabar of كان.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «إذا جاء نصر الله والفتح» there is an implicit, derivative metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya tabaʿiyya): what is decreed, namely the victory and the conquest, is likened to a living being walking, heading from eternity to its appointed time. So arrival is likened to coming, the thing likened to is omitted, and one of its characteristics is taken, namely coming.
Imam al-Rāzī has given a delightful passage, which we give you below because of its value and benefit. He said: "The Companions agreed that this surah indicated the announcement of the death of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, for several reasons:
First: they knew it when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ delivered a sermon after the surah and mentioned the choice, which was his saying ﷺ in his sermon when this surah was sent down: 'A servant was given a choice by Allah the Exalted between this world and meeting Him, and he chose meeting Allah the Exalted.' Abū Bakr said: 'May our souls, our wealth, our fathers and our children be your ransom.'
Second: that when He mentioned the arrival [Translator's note: the source reads "حصور", evidently a misprint for "حصول"] of the victory and the conquest and people entering the religion in crowds, this indicated the attainment of perfection, and completion is followed by decline and deficiency, as has been said:
إذا تمّ أمر بدا نقصه ... توقع زوالا إذا قيل تم
(When a matter is complete, its deficiency appears; expect its passing when it is said "complete".)
Third: that Allah the Exalted commanded him to glorify, praise and seek forgiveness, and his being occupied with that prevents him from being occupied with the affairs of the community, so this was like an alert that the matter of conveying the message was complete and perfected, and that requires the fulfilment of the appointed term; for had he ﷺ remained after that, he would have been like one dismissed from the message, and that is not permissible."

farraa:1-2.t:
His words: ﴿إِذَا جَآءَ نَصْرُ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلْفَتْحُ﴾.
Meaning the conquest of Mecca. ﴿وَرَأَيْتَ ٱلنَّاسَ يَدْخُلُونَ فِي دِينِ ٱللَّهِ أَفْوَاجاً﴾.
He says: and you saw the tribes, a whole tribe accepting Islam at once; before that, a man would accept Islam only after another man. [Translator's note: the source has «وقيل ذلك», apparently for «وقبل ذلك» (before that); translated by the latter.]

farraa:3-3.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ﴾.
He says: then pray. And they mentioned that he ﷺ said when this surah was revealed: My own death has been announced to me.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: «إذا»: adverbial and conditional, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the meaning of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) «سبِّح».

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The clause «يدخلون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الناس, and «أفواجًا» is a ḥāl from the wāw.

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The preposition «بحمد» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «سَبِّح», and the clause «إنه كان توابا» is resumptive.

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, Exalted is He (إذا جاء نصر الله): the governing word (ʿāmil) in (إذا) is (جاء); its explanation has already preceded.

mekki-muskil:2-2.t:
His saying (يدخلون): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (الناس), because (رأيت) is from seeing with the eye.
His saying (أفواجا): accusative as a ḥāl from the latent pronoun in (يدخلون), and that is what governs it. (أفواج) is the plural of «فوج», and its analogical [plural] is «أفواج», because the ḍamma is felt to be heavy on the wāw, so they likened «فَعْل» to «فِعْل» and pluralised it with the plural of ... [Translator's note: the text appears corrupt and incomplete here: «وقياسه أفواج» is presumably «وقياسه أفوُج» (its analogical plural would be «أفعُل»), and the final sentence breaks off after «جمع».]

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb (ẓarf) of future time containing the meaning of condition, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿سبح﴾.
﴿جاء﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; the clause جاء is in the position of the genitive (majrūr) because the adverb is put in construct with it.
﴿نصر الله﴾: نصر: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma, and it is muḍāf; the word of majesty is muḍāf ilayhi, genitive by the kasra. The maṣdar (verbal noun) ﴿نصر﴾ is put in construct with its agent, and its object is omitted, i.e. "Allah's help to you and to the believers".
﴿والفتح﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and الفتح is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to ﴿نصر﴾, nominative by the ḍamma.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿ورأيت﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; رأيت: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, and the tāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the fatḥa in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ) as fāʿil (agent). The clause ﴿رأيت﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿جاء﴾ and is in the position of the genitive; the seeing is either visual or cognitive.
﴿الناس﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa; it is the first object if the seeing is cognitive.
﴿يدخلون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw of the plural is a pronoun in the position of the nominative as fāʿil. The clause ﴿يدخلون﴾ is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) of الناس if ﴿رأيت﴾ is visual; and if the seeing is cognitive, the clause is in the position of the accusative as the second object of ﴿رأيت﴾.
﴿في دين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يدخلون﴾.
﴿الله﴾: the word of majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.
﴿أفواجا﴾: ḥāl, accusative by the fatḥa, from the agent of يدخلون, which is the wāw of the plural.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿فسبح﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); سبح is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, and its fāʿil (agent) is necessarily latent (mustatir) in it, its implied form being "أنت". The clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of ﴿إذا﴾.
﴿بحمد﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of سبح, i.e. "clothed with the praise of your Lord"; and حمد is muḍāf.
﴿ربك﴾: رب is muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra, and it is muḍāf; the kāf of address is a pronoun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿واستغفره﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; استغفره is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, and its agent is necessarily latent in it, its implied form being "أنت"; the hāʾ is a pronoun in the position of the accusative (manṣūb) as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause ﴿استغفره﴾ has no grammatical position because it is conjoined to the clause of the apodosis of the non-jussive condition, ﴿سبح﴾.
﴿إنه﴾: إن is an abrogating particle, indeclinable on the fatḥa, with no grammatical position; the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of the accusative as the noun of إن.
﴿كان﴾: an incomplete past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa; the noun of كان is latent, its implied form being "هو".
﴿توابا﴾: the khabar (predicate) of كان, accusative by the fatḥa. The clause ﴿كان توابا﴾ is in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ) as the khabar of إن, and the clause ﴿إنه كان توابا﴾ is causal (taʿlīliyya) and has no grammatical position.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: إِذا is an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān), accusative by جاء. نَصْرُ اللَّهِ is nominative by جاء (as its agent); (نصر) has the plural anṣār, and by analogy (it should be) anṣur. وَالْفَتْحُ is conjoined to it.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: وَرَأَيْتَ النَّاسَ يَدْخُلُونَ: «يدخلون» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), or as the predicate (second object) of رأيت. أَفْواجاً is accusative as a ḥāl, the plural of fawj; by analogy, fawj (should have the plural) afwuj, but the vowel on the wāw was felt to be heavy, so they likened faʿl to fiʿl [Translator's note: i.e., gave it the plural pattern afʿāl].

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ, i.e., make your glorification with praise. وَاسْتَغْفِرْهُ: and he ﷺ used to say: «I seek Allah's forgiveness a hundred times in the day and the night». إِنَّهُ كانَ تَوَّاباً: (توابا is) the khabar (predicate) of كان, and the clause is the khabar of إنّ. There was in this sūra an indication of his prophethood ﷺ, because it was revealed before the Conquest. Ibn ʿAbbās said: so he knew that when the Conquest came… so we counted (it as a sign of) his appointed term ﷺ [Translator's note: the sentence is disjointed in the text]. Qatāda said: the sūra of the Conquest, إِذا جاءَ نَصْرُ اللَّهِ, was revealed in Medina.

safi-cedvel:1-3.t:
* I'rab:
(في دين) is attached to (يدخلون). (أفواجا) is an accusative ḥāl from the agent of يدخلون. (the fāʾ) is the connecting fāʾ of the apodosis. (بحمد) is attached to a ḥāl from the agent of سبّح, i.e. "being engaged in the praise of"..
Clause: «جاء نصر الله» is in the position of genitive, as muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «رأيت ... » is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause جاء نصر ...
And the clause: «يدخلون ... » is in the position of accusative, a ḥāl from الناس [Note: or a second direct object if the seeing is of the heart.].
And the clause: «سبّح ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause: «استغفره ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause سبّح.
And the clause: «إنّه كان توابا ... » has no grammatical position; it is causal.
And the clause: «كان توّابا» is in the position of nominative, the khabar of إنّ.

* Rhetoric:
Al-istiʿāra al-makniyya (implicit metaphor): in His saying, the Exalted: «إِذا جاءَ نَصْرُ اللَّهِ وَالْفَتْحُ».
Here the decreed thing, namely the victory and the conquest, is likened to a living being walking, directed from eternity to its appointed time; so the occurrence is likened to coming, the thing likened to is omitted, and one of its characteristics, namely coming, is taken.

* Benefits:
- Knowledge raises its possessor:
On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, used to admit me with the elders of Badr. Some of them said: Why does this youth enter with us? He said: He is one of those whom you know. He said: One day he called them and called me with them, then said: What do you say about the saying of Allah the Exalted (إِذا جاءَ نَصْرُ اللَّهِ وَالْفَتْحُ) to the end of the sūra? Some of them said: We were commanded to praise Allah and ask His forgiveness when we are given victory and a conquest is opened for us; and some were silent and said nothing. He said to me: Is that what you say, O Ibn ʿAbbās? I said: No. He said: Then what is it? I said: It is the term of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, which He informed him of: (إِذا جاءَ نَصْرُ اللَّهِ وَالْفَتْحُ) – that is the sign of your term – (فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ وَاسْتَغْفِرْهُ إِنَّهُ كانَ تَوَّاباً). ʿUmar said: I know nothing of it except what you know.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: When this sūra was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ knew that his own death had been announced to him.

semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {نَصْرُ الله}: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in construct with its agent; its object is omitted because the meaning is understood, i.e. Allah's help to you and the believers. Likewise the objects of «الفتح» and what it is attached to: "and the opening", i.e. the opening of the lands to you and your community. Or what is intended is: "when these two acts come", without regard to what they are attached to, as in His saying: {أَمَاتَ وَأَحْيَا} [al-Najm: 44]. The al- in «الفتح» is a substitute for the construct (iḍāfa), i.e. "and His opening", according to the Kufans; according to the Basrans the referring pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, i.e. "and the opening from Him", because [the context] indicates that. What governs «إذا» is either «جاء» — this is Makkī's view, and the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] inclined to it and supported it in several places; this was given before as I transmitted it from Makkī and from him — or, second, it is «فَسَبِّحْ», to which al-Zamakhsharī and al-Ḥawfī inclined. The Shaykh rejected this from both of them on the ground that what comes after the fāʾ of the apodosis does not govern what comes before it. There is a discussion of this, part of which was given in Sūrat «والضُّحى».

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {يَدْخُلُونَ}: it is either a ḥāl (circumstantial), if «رَأَيْتَ» is visual — in al-Zamakhsharī's wording: "if it is in the sense of 'you beheld' or 'you knew (ʿarafta)'"; the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] disputed this with him, [saying] that raʾayta is not known to be in the sense of ʿarafta; he said: "So that needs verification" — or it is a second object, if it is in the sense of ʿalimta, transitive to two objects. This is the reading of the generality, I mean «يَدْخُلون» in the active. Ibn Kathīr, in one transmission, read «يُدْخَلون» in the passive. «في دين» is a figurative adverb of place, and it is an eloquent, effective figure here.
His saying: {أَفْوَاجاً}: a ḥāl from the agent of «يَدْخُلون». Makkī said: "Its analogical [plural] is afwuj, except that the ḍamma is felt heavy on the wāw, so they likened faʿl — meaning with sukūn — to faʿal — meaning with fatḥa — and gave it its plural." — end of quote. I.e. faʿl with sukūn has as its analogical [plural] afʿul, like fals and aflus, except that the ḍamma on the wāw was felt heavy, so they gave it the plural of faʿal with a vowelled middle, like jamal and ajmāl; because faʿl with sukūn [pluralised] on afʿāl is not analogical when the faʿl is sound, as in farkh and afrākh, zand and aznād — many words of this kind are attested, yet they did not make it a rule. Al-Ḥawfī said something of this.
His saying: {بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ}: a ḥāl, i.e. accompanied by His praise. The verification of this was given in al-Baqara at His saying: {وَنَحْنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِكَ} [al-Baqara: 30].

ukberi-tibyan:2-2.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَرَأَيْتَ النَّاسَ يَدْخُلُونَ فِي دِينِ اللَّهِ أَفْوَاجًا (٢)).
The words of the Exalted (يَدْخُلُونَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «النَّاسَ». (أَفْوَاجًا) is a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) in «يَدْخُلُونَ».

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Naṣr
Medinan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إذا جاءَ نَصْرُ اللَّهِ والفَتْحُ﴾ ("when the help of Allah and the victory come"): it was said that the victory, as has come in the exegesis, [means] that the Prophet's ﷺ own death was announced to him in this sūra: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, let him know that when the conquest of Mecca came and people entered Islam in crowds, his appointed term ﷺ had drawn near. He used to say that: «”إنَّهُ قَدْ نُعِيَتْ إلَيَّ نَفْسِي في هَذِهِ السُّورَةِ“» ("my death has been announced to me in this sūra"). So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, commanded him to increase glorification and seeking forgiveness, so that He might seal for him, at the end of his life, with an increase in righteous deeds, by following what He commanded him.

zajjaj:2-2.t: ﴿وَرَأيْتَ النّاسَ يَدْخُلُونَ في دِينِ اللَّهِ أفْواجًا﴾ ("and you see people entering the religion of Allah in crowds"): the meaning of ﴿أفْواجًا﴾ is large groups; that is, after they used to enter one by one and two by two, the tribe came to enter Islam in its entirety.
